# Coin Silver Standards

Different national mints settled on different silver standards, and the
terminology is a frequent source of confusion in auction listings.

Sterling silver is 92.5% silver and 7.5% copper, the standard used for
British coinage until 1920. "Coin silver" in the American usage means a
90% silver alloy.

Morgan dollars were struck in sterling, 92.5% silver, which is why they
tone so readily compared to later clad issues. Trade dollars used a
slightly heavier planchet to compete with the Mexican eight reales in
Asian markets.

After 1965 the United States removed silver from circulating dimes and
quarters entirely, leaving only collector strikes in precious metal.

Related: [[Morgan Dollar]], [[Seated Liberty Dollar]].
